drivingQuestion: In what kind of impurity do R' Shimon and the Rabbis disagree?
outcomeNote: The positions are given in the next unit.

segments.he: נוּמִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל כּוּ׳. אִיתְּמַר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא – חַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא;
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Shimon stated» a ruling in which he «deems» one «liable» for eating in a state of ritual impurity an item «whose» typical «manner» is such that one «eats» it, but not for eating the wood, the frankincense, or the incense, whose typical manner is such that one does not eat it. The Rabbis disagree and deem him liable in all these cases. It «was stated» that two pairs of amora’im disagreed with regard to this issue; one pair is «Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish,» and the other pair is «Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina.» The two different opinions that follow were respectively stated by «one of this pair and one of that pair.»
